subject.title: [Bug]: Task and Memory Recall Is Often Too Weak to Trust Across Real Conversations

question: What durable memory contract should OpenClaw promise for personal assistants: default project/task state, opt-in session transcript recall, Active Memory-managed state, or a narrower same-assistant private recall model?
rationale: The requested behavior spans defaults, privacy, transcript visibility, plugin boundaries, and agent-owned summarization, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent user-facing memory model.

options.title: Define a narrow private-recall contract
options.body: Use #99611 as the first product slice and make same-assistant private conversations recallable with explicit visibility and privacy rules before broader project/task semantics.

options.title: Keep recall opt-in and plugin-owned
options.body: Leave current defaults unchanged and document Active Memory/sessionMemory as optional advanced features rather than promising default durable task memory.

options.title: Design a full project/task memory layer
options.body: Create a larger product track for canonical project/task files, open-task state, live gates, and migrations before implementation.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow private-recall contract
recommendation.body: Use #99611 as the first product slice and make same-assistant private conversations recallable with explicit visibility and privacy rules before broader project/task semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Their open #99611 proposal is the closest visible maintainer-owned product decision for the same-assistant private recall boundary.
